HelpProgressLabel: 10 steps • Quick guide to Tune Master
HelpStep0Text:
The top bar of the main window contains all display controls — adjust these first for a comfortable experience.

• Language: Русский / English — switches the entire interface.
• Font «+» / «−» — changes the font size across the whole app (results, charts, part lists). Size is saved and restored on restart.
• Units: Metric ↔ Imperial — toggles all displayed values (speeds, pressures, lengths, spring rates).
• Power unit: HP / PS / kW — independent from the metric/imperial toggle.
• Spring-rate unit: N/mm · kgf/mm · lb/in — displayed on results and charts.
HelpStep0Note: All internal calculations always run in metric (SI) units. Units and language switches only affect the displayed text — the underlying physics are unchanged. Font size, selected units and language are persisted to %APPDATA%\ForzaTuneMaster\settings.json.
HelpStep1Text:
Top-left, in the 'Car search' box, start typing a make, model or year — the list filters automatically. Pick a car from the dropdown.

All specs (mass, weight distribution, power, torque, RPM, engine, drive type, gear count, wheelbase, tires, etc.) fill in automatically from the built-in game database. The '✕' button clears the selection.
HelpStep1Note: The entire car and parts database is bundled with the app and extracted directly from Forza Horizon 6 game files — no internet and no manual spec entry needed. The selected car appears in the header of the results panel on the right.
HelpStep2Text:
Below the search box are collapsible upgrade sections — just like the in-game garage. Click a header to expand a section:

• Body kits & modifications (swaps)
• Engine
• Chassis & handling
• Drivetrain
• Tires & wheels
• Aero & appearance

Each section offers exactly the parts that exist for the selected car in the game.
HelpStep2Note: Part lists are built from the selected car's database; categories that don't apply auto-hide. Changing any part recalculates power, mass, drive type and geometry, and the tune updates automatically.
HelpStep3Text:
The 'Body kits & modifications' section holds the swaps: engine, drivetrain (FWD/RWD/AWD) and aspiration type — these reshape the whole power map and car behavior.

The 'Engine' section is grouped: valvetrain & bottom end (camshaft, displacement, valves, pistons, flywheel), air/fuel/exhaust (intake, manifold, exhaust, fuel system, intercooler, restrictor) and ignition/cooling.
HelpStep3Note: For electric cars the ICE sections hide — a 'Motor & battery' section appears instead, with a motor swap and its upgrades. Hybrids and ICE cars use the engine sections.
HelpStep4Text:
• CHASSIS — springs/dampers, anti-roll bars (front/rear), brakes, chassis stiffness, weight reduction.
• DRIVETRAIN — gearbox, clutch, final drive/driveline, differential.
• TIRES & WHEELS — tire compound, width and profile (front/rear), wheel style and size, track spacers.
• AERO — front bumper, rear wing, rear bumper, side skirts.
HelpStep4Note:
The level of the installed parts sets the physical tuning bounds: the generator picks values within the range that the chosen parts unlock (e.g. race springs give a wider stiffness and ride-height range).

⚠ Wheels (rim style) — approximate: their effect on car mass is estimated from the wheel's lightness tier (an empirical formula), not taken directly from the game. Rim size and tire width are exact. It is a difference of a few kg, so it has a negligible effect on the tuning calculations.
HelpStep5Text:
At the bottom of the results panel (right), choose a discipline — it drives target spring frequencies, wheel geometry, gear ratios, differential and tire pressure:

• Road • Touge • Rally • Cross Country • Drift • Drag • Street

Next to it, pick a season (Spring / Summer / Autumn / Winter). For Drag, also set the distance (¼, ½ or mile).
HelpStep5Note: There is no separate 'Generate' button — the tune recalculates automatically on any change: car selection, a part swap, discipline or season. Season changes the grip factor and adjusts springs, dampers, ARB, differential and tire pressure.
HelpStep6Text: The right panel shows the finished tune. The colored bar under each value shows where it sits within its allowed range. Results are split into sections:
HelpStep7Text:
In Drag mode a '🚦 LAUNCH CONTROL' block appears above the gears with the optimal launch RPM. Hold the throttle at this RPM before launching.

The calculation accounts for: aspiration type (turbos need pre-spooling), torque-peak RPM (lower peak = lower launch), drive type (AWD can launch at higher RPM) and fuel type (diesel gets lower RPM).
HelpStep8Text:
Profiles save a full build: car, installed parts, discipline/season and the result.

• '💾 Save' — stores the current build. Name auto-generated: Make_Model_Year_Drive_Discipline.
• 'Load' — pick a profile in the list below and it applies instantly.
• '🗑 Delete' — removes the selected profile.
• 'Delete all' — clears the whole profile list.

Profiles are stored as JSON in %APPDATA%\ForzaTuneMaster\profiles\ and are recalculated automatically on load when needed.
HelpStep8Note:
Units and language toggle in the top bar:
• Metric / Imperial — affects all unit displays
• Power: HP / PS / kW
• Spring rate: N/mm · kgf/mm · lb/in
• Interface language: Русский / English
• «+» / «−» buttons — font size across the whole app (charts included). Size is saved.

All calculations run in metric (SI) units — imperial conversion is for display only.
HelpStep9Text:
Tune results can be shown in a separate window on top of the game and other apps:

• TOGGLE — the 'Overlay' checkbox in the results panel header or Ctrl+Shift+O
• DRAG — by the window header
• RESIZE — by any corner of the window
• OPACITY — slider in the header
• CLOSE — the ✕ button in the header or press Ctrl+Shift+O again

Overlay position, size and opacity are saved and restored on next open.

💡 When you change the car or a part, the overlay charts (just like in the main window) update smoothly: fade-out → redraw → fade-in. Language/unit switches redraw instantly.
HelpStep6Line1: • TIRE PRESSURE — front/rear. Base from tire compound, adjusted by mass and weight distribution.
HelpStep6Line2: • WHEEL ALIGNMENT — camber (discipline + load + aero), caster (mass + speed), toe (drive + discipline + speed).
HelpStep6Line3: • ANTI-ROLL BARS (ARB) — front/rear stiffness. From discipline, mass, track, weight distribution and body roll.
HelpStep6Line4: • SPRINGS + RIDE HEIGHT — stiffness from target frequency (k = 0.0197 × Hz² × mass × wtDist) within the chosen springs' physics. Height: from discipline and engine position.
HelpStep6Line5: • DAMPERS — rebound/bump (1–20). Base from discipline, adjusted for mass, weight dist, drive type and aspiration.
HelpStep6Line6: • AERODYNAMICS — front/rear downforce. Depends on drive type, speed and power; solved iteratively. Drift/CC/Rally are reduced.
HelpStep6Line7: • DIFFERENTIAL — accel/decel lock. From discipline/drive, power and torque. For AWD — separate front and center diff.
HelpStep6Line8: • BRAKES — balance (% front) = weight dist + discipline offset. Pressure: from discipline, mass and speed.
HelpStep6Line9: • GEARING — final drive targeting max speed, ratios (geometric progression) with post-validation. First/top gear from discipline.
HelpStep6Line10: Hover over any value — the tooltip explains the physics. Below: the gear chart (speed range per gear) with a legend (trajectory, rev limit, max speed) and the power/torque curve. The '!' badge next to springs warns that values may exceed in-game limits. Next to final drive — recommended gear count with a force-recalc checkbox. The checkboxes show/hide the charts. Charts animate smoothly when data changes.
ChartPeakToleranceHint: Calculated values. May differ slightly from in-game due to curve scaling mechanics and approximation.

Expl_TirePressureReason_Drift: Drift: ~25 PSI front / ~22 PSI rear for predictable sliding.
Expl_TirePressureReason_Rally: Rally/CC: lower pressure for maximum contact patch.
Expl_TirePressureReason_CrossCountry: Rally/CC: lower pressure for maximum contact patch.
Expl_TirePressureReason_Touge: Touge: slightly softer than base for mountain road grip.
Expl_TirePressureReason_Street: Street: standard pressure with slight rear margin for maneuvers.
Expl_CamberReason_Drag: Drag: minimal camber — maximum contact patch at launch.
Expl_CamberReason_Drift: Drift: aggressive front camber for control at high steering angles.
Expl_CamberReason_Rally: Rally: moderate camber — flat contact patch on gravel.
Expl_CamberReason_CrossCountry: CC: minimal camber — maximum contact on bumps.
Expl_CamberReason_Touge: Touge: increased camber for precise corner entry on tight turns.
Expl_CamberReason_Road: Road: classic negative camber to compensate for body roll in corners.
Expl_ARBNote_Drag: Drag: min front for weight transfer; stiff rear for platform.
Expl_ARBNote_DriftRWD: Drift: soft front for initiation; moderate rear for angle hold (ForzaFire R20-25).
Expl_ARBNote_Rally: Rally: soft for independent wheel travel on gravel.
Expl_ARBNote_CrossCountry: CC: min stiffness for suspension articulation.
Expl_ARBNote_TougeRWD: Touge RWD: stiffer for precise control.
Expl_ARBNote_TougeFWD: Touge FWD: soft front for grip, stiff rear for rotation.
Expl_ARBNote_StreetFWD: Street FWD: soft front for grip, stiffer rear against understeer.
Expl_ARBNote_RoadRWD: Road RWD: front stiffer than rear for precise entry (ForzaFire F18-28/R12-20).
Expl_ARBNote_RoadFWD: Road FWD: soft front (grip), stiffer rear (rotation).
Expl_ARBNote_RoadAWD: Road AWD: F26/R33 — balanced ARBs (ForzaFire F22-30/R28-38).
